target_hardware: Intel HD 5500 (Broadwell GT2), 8GB System RAM, Windows 10/11 x64

metrics.runtime_cpu_cost: Zero (pre-baked static triangle vertices and normals)
metrics.notes: Ideal for resource-constrained systems. Zero runtime raycast computation; instant rendering.

metrics.runtime_cpu_cost: Moderate on authoring (three-mesh-bvh picking); Low in viewer mode
metrics.notes: Excellent authoring workflow. BVH tree build takes ~120ms at startup, then gives fast interactive picking.

metrics.runtime_cpu_cost: Ultra-low (pure analytical math for HULL; no mesh raycasting)
metrics.notes: Extremely fast load time (724ms) and low heap (32MB). Perfect fallback when complex skin meshes fail to load.

metrics.runtime_cpu_cost: High on init (5-step directional-cone raycast per point) + Draco decompression
metrics.notes: Draco WASM decoder + React 19 increases heap to 82.4MB and startup to 3.4s on Intel HD 5500.

recommendation: Adopt JICio pre-baked static surface coordinates for runtime production viewing (zero CPU overhead, 42MB heap), coupled with Meridian Studio's three-mesh-bvh CatmullRom ribbon curves for interactive authoring/calibration.
